title: Patch, skim and finishing coats
audience: Plasterers who patch and finish walls and ceilings and are paid for the higher-rate finishing work
learningOutcomes: Apply a patch and a skim coat in layers suited to the depth and the finish.
Allow each layer to dry before the next is applied, and check the drying.
Finish a skim to a flat, even surface that is ready for paint.

instruction.heading: Layers and drying
instruction.body: A plaster repair is built in layers. Deep patches are filled in lifts, each thinner than the last, and each lift is allowed to stiffen before the next. A thin skim coat is applied last, over a sound and dry base. Applying a thick layer in one go traps moisture, cracks as it shrinks, and may not bond. Drying takes longer in cold and damp conditions, and the surface must be dry before paint is applied. Check the drying by the colour and the feel of the surface, and by the data sheet time.

instruction.heading: Finishing a skim
instruction.body: Apply the skim with a flat trowel, working in short passes that overlap. Work from a light source across the wall so that high and low spots show. Let the skim firm enough to be worked, and then finish with a damp trowel or sponge, working from the centre toward the edges. A skim that is worked too early pulls off; a skim that is left too long shows trowel marks. Check the finished surface with a straight edge and under a raking light before it is painted.

procedure: Check the base is sound, dry and bonded, and that any movement has been referred.
Fill deep patches in lifts, allowing each lift to stiffen before the next.
Apply the skim in short overlapping passes over the dry base.
Work the skim to the stage the data sheet describes, and finish with a damp trowel or sponge.
Check the finish with a straight edge and under a raking light.
Allow the surface to dry fully before any paint is applied, and record the drying time.

workedExamples.situation: A deep patch on a ceiling is filled in one thick layer on the same day, and the client asks for paint the next morning.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the ceiling be painted the next morning?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. A thick single layer may not dry through, and it can crack as it shrinks. Fill the patch in lifts, allow drying, and check the surface is dry before painting. Record the drying time and tell the client when painting can start.

equipmentAndPpe: Flat trowels and a straight edge
Dust mask suited to the task

commonErrors.error: Applying a deep patch in one thick layer.
commonErrors.prevention: Fill in lifts and allow each lift to stiffen.

commonErrors.error: Painting before the plaster is dry.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the drying by the data sheet and the surface, and record it.

commonErrors.error: Working the skim too early or too late.
commonErrors.prevention: Work the skim at the stage the data sheet describes.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: New South Wales: dry plastering and wet plastering each need a contractor licence above $5,000 of labour and materials, GST included (NSW Government pages, last updated 23 June 2026).
Queensland: plastering solid and plastering drywall are QBCC classes (both pages last reviewed 31 August 2021).
Completing this lesson does not give a plastering or rendering licence, certificate or authority.

qualityStandard: Each layer is dry and bonded before the next is applied.
The finished skim is flat under a straight edge and free of trowel marks under raking light.
Paint is applied only after the drying time is recorded and the surface is dry.
documentationEvidence: Patch and skim record with layers, drying times and product used
summary: Fill deep repairs in lifts and allow each to dry.
Work the skim at the right stage and finish with a damp trowel.
Check the finish with a straight edge and under raking light before painting.

knowledgeChecks.question: A deep ceiling patch is filled in one thick layer and painting is planned for the next morning. What is correct?
options: Paint the next morning, since the surface will be dry enough by then
Thin the paint to cover the wet plaster quickly before it dries out
Fill in lifts, allow drying, and paint only when the surface is dry
Skip the skim coat and paint straight over the patch to save time

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a finished skim be checked?
options: By touch only, along the whole wall surface
By painting a test square and looking at it
It is not necessary to check the finish at all
With a straight edge and under a raking light

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the lesson say a deep patch is filled?
options: In one thick layer to save time
In lifts, each thinner than the last
With paint, to seal the hole
